gilmoretyrannus:eswiki:7.title: Nanotyrannus (Controversia: T. rex inmaduro o género separado)

facts.statement: Gilmoretyrannus is a newly named genus and combination of a tyrannosauroid dinosaur described by Sancarlo and Paul.
facts.quote: Novelty: Gen. et comb. nov

facts.statement: The type locality of Gilmoretyrannus is the Lance and Hell Creek formations in Montana and Wyoming, United States.
facts.quote: Type locality: Lance and Hell Creek formations

facts.statement: Gilmoretyrannus lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is a tyrannosauroid dinosaur whose fossil range is the Late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Maastrichtian

facts.statement: The genus Nanotyrannus was formally named by Bakker, Williams and Currie in 1988.
facts.quote: authority: Bakker, Williams & Currie, 1988

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived in western North America about 67 million years ago during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: lived in what is now western North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, 67 million years ago

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus fossils are primarily known from the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: Its fossils are mainly known from the Hell Creek Formation

facts.statement: The first species, N. lancensis, was originally described as a new species of Gorgosaurus by Charles W. Gilmore in 1946 based on a single skull.
facts.quote: first named species, N. lancensis, was described as a new species of Gorgosaurus in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore based on a single skull

facts.statement: Many researchers consider the Nanotyrannus skull to belong to an immature Tyrannosaurus rex, making its taxonomic status controversial.
facts.quote: Subsequent research indicated that the skull belonged to an immature animal, leading many researchers to favor its identification as a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had a slender, low skull with small crests or horns in front of the eyes, unlike the robust skull of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus had a slender, low skull, and small crests or horns immediately in front of its eyes

facts.statement: Large muscle‑attachment sites at the back of the Nanotyrannus skull suggest it could flex its head strongly side‑to‑side.
facts.quote: muscle attachment sites at the back of its skull were large, suggesting that it could strongly flex its head from side to side

facts.statement: Longer legs and relatively larger forelimbs indicate Nanotyrannus was likely a pursuit predator.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was longer-legged than contemporary taxa, suggesting that it was a pursuit predator, and had forelimbs which were both absolutely and proportionally larger than its relatives

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is the sole confirmed member of the family Nanotyrannidae, though some phylogenetic analyses link it with Appalachiosaurus and Dryptosaurus.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus is the only definite representative of the family Nanotyrannidae, though one phylogenetic hypothesis suggests close relations to Appalachiosaurus and Dryptosaurus

facts.statement: The holotype skull CMNH 7541 was collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle and described by Gilmore in 1946 as Gorgosaurus lancensis.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus is based on CMNH 7541, a skull collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle. It was described in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore, who classified it as a new species in the tyrannosaurid genus Gorgosaurus, G. lancensis

facts.statement: The first suggestion that the Nanotyrannus holotype might be a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex was made by Rozhdestvensky in 1965.
facts.quote: The possibility that the holotype represents a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex was first suggested by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky in 1965

facts.statement: Thomas Carr's 1999 analysis concluded the specimen was immature, influencing many paleontologists to view it as a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Subsequent analysis of the specimen by Thomas Carr in 1999 indicated that it was immature, leading Carr and many other paleontologists to consider it a juvenile specimen of T. rex

facts.statement: The juvenile tyrannosaur specimen "Jane" (BMRP 2002.4.1) was discovered in 2001 and was initially thought to belong to Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: In 2001, a more complete juvenile tyrannosaur (nicknamed "Jane", accession number BMRP 2002.4.1), suggested to belong to the same species as the original Nanotyrannus specimen, was uncovered

facts.statement: A 2005 conference at the Burpee Museum focused on the validity of Nanotyrannus after the discovery of "Jane".
facts.quote: prompted a conference on tyrannosaurs focused on the issues of the validity of Nanotyrannus, held at the Burpee Museum of Natural History in 2005

facts.statement: Sancarlo and Paul proposed moving Nanotyrannus lethaeus to a new genus named Gilmoretyrannus, creating the combination Gilmoretyrannus lethaeus.
facts.quote: Sancarlo & Paul suggested that N. lethaeus should be placed in a genus distinct from Nanotyrannus, which they named Gilmoretyrannus, creating the new combination Gilmoretyrannus lethaeus.

facts.statement: A later estimate gave a greater total length of about 6 m.
facts.quote: later estimate suggested a greater length of 6 m

facts.statement: Body‑mass estimates for the genus are 703.78 kg for N. lancensis (specimen NCSM 40000) and over 833 kg for N. lethaeus (holotype BMRP 2002.4.1).
facts.quote: Zanno and Napoli provided body mass estimates of 703.78 kg for N. lancensis (specifically NCSM 40000) and over 833 kg for N. lethaeus (the holotype, BMRP 2002.4.1)

facts.statement: If fully grown, N. lethaeus may have weighed around 1,200 kg.
facts.quote: adult N. lethaeus may have weighed around 1200 kg

facts.statement: The maximum possible body mass for the genus has been estimated at roughly 1,500 kg.
facts.quote: maximum body mass of the genus may have been approximately 1500 kg

facts.statement: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) measures 57.2 cm from the front of the premaxilla to the rear of the quadrate.
facts.quote: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) of Nanotyrannus measures 57.2 cm when measured from the anterior (front) tip of the premaxilla to the posterior (rear) tip of the quadrate

facts.statement: Specimen NCSM 40000 has a skull length of 71.3 cm and a maximum width of 27.3 cm.
facts.quote: That of NCSM 40000 measures 71.3 cm in length, and has a maximum width of 27.3 cm

facts.statement: All known specimens of Nanotyrannus lack the subnarial foramen that is present in many other tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: this is absent in every specimen of Nanotyrannus

facts.statement: In N. lancensis the lateral surface of the subnarial process faces dorsolaterally, unlike the dorsomedial orientation seen in Daspletosaurus and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: the lateral (outer) surface of the subnarial process faces dorsolaterally (upwards and outwards) in N. lancensis. In contrast, this process faces dorsomedially (upwards and towards the midline) in Daspletosaurus and Tyrannosaurus

facts.statement: The nasal bones of the animal are partially fused and bear large, well‑developed processes on their posterolateral surfaces.
facts.quote: The nasal bones are partly fused, with large, well-developed processes on their posterolateral (rearward and to the side) surfaces

facts.statement: The postorbital bone of Nanotyrannus lacks a cornual process, which is unusual among eutyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The postorbital bone has no cornual process, which is unusual among eutyrannosaurs, as even young tyrannosaurids had one.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lacks a lateral fossa on the postorbital process of its jugal bone, unlike Bistahieversor, Daspletosaurus, Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Unlike Bistahieversor, Daspletosaurus, Tarbosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus, the jugal of Nanotyrannus lacks a lateral fossa on its postorbital process.

facts.statement: The parietal bone of Nanotyrannus bears a thin sagittal crest that expands posteriorly into a large nuchal crest lacking parasagittal fossae.
facts.quote: The parietal bone has a thin sagittal crest, expanding posteriorly into a large nuchal crest; this crest lacks the parasagittal fossae present in the nuchal crests of both Albertosaurus and Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus has a deep keel on the ventral portion of the vomer and the bone is lance‑shaped rather than diamond‑shaped.
facts.quote: The vomer has a deep keel on its ventral portion, similar to Daspletosaurus, and is lance-shaped rather than diamond-shaped as in more derived tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The basitubera of Nanotyrannus are strongly laterally expanded, indicating the head could be flexed strongly sideways.
facts.quote: The basitubera (muscle attachment sites at the back of the head) of Nanotyrannus were strongly laterally expanded, suggesting that the head could be strongly flexed sideways.

facts.statement: The most anterior maxillary tooth of Nanotyrannus was small and resembled the premaxillary teeth, a trait shared with many other tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: Unlike Daspletosaurus, Tarbosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus, but like many other tyrannosauroids, the most anterior tooth of each maxilla was small and resembled those of the premaxillae.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had ziphodont (serrated) maxillary teeth, unlike most tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Unlike most tyrannosaurids, the maxillary teeth were ziphodont.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had proportionally very large arms, more similar in size to those of basal tyrannosauroids than to later tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The arms of Nanotyrannus are proportionally very large, proportionally more similar to basal tyrannosauroids than to those of tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The distal end of the humerus of Nanotyrannus bears five tubercles, a feature not seen in other eutyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The distal (further from the body) end of the humerus (upper arm bone) of Nanotyrannus bears five tubercles, unlike other eutyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: The first metacarpal of Nanotyrannus was subtriangular and reduced, unlike the condition in tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The first metacarpal is subtriangular and reduced, unlike tyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: In Nanotyrannus lethaeus the fourth trochanter is parallel to the femoral shaft and does not form a peak.
facts.quote: the fourth trochanter, (structure to which the caudofemoralis muscle attaches), is parallel to the femoral shaft, and in N. lethaeus does not form a peak.

facts.statement: The hypercursorial hind limbs of Nanotyrannus suggest a lifestyle adapted to pursuit predation.
facts.quote: The extreme proportions of their "hypercursorial" hind limbs may correlate to a different lifestyle from tyrannosaurids, one adapted more toward pursuit predation.

facts.statement: Maximum‑parsimony analysis placed Moros intrepidus as the sister taxon to the Nanotyrannus lethaeus holotype ("Jane").
facts.quote: The first, a maximum parsimony analysis (shown below as Topology A) recovered the 'mid'-Cretaceous taxon Moros intrepidus as the sister taxon to the Nanoyrannus lethaeus holotype ("Jane", BMRP 2002.4.1)

facts.statement: Bayesian inference analysis placed Moros outside Nanotyrannidae as a non‑eutyrannosaurian sister to Timurlengia.
facts.quote: the second, a Bayesian inference analysis implementing a fossilized birth–death (BI-FBD) model (shown below as Topology B), placed Moros outside as a non-eutyrannosaurian as the sister to Timurlengia.

facts.statement: The most recent common ancestor of Nanotyrannidae and Tyrannosauridae may have lived about 103 million years ago, around the formation of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) between Nanotyrannidae and Tyrannosauridae may have lived roughly 103 million years ago, around the time of the formation of the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was a medium‑sized tyrannosauroid that grew to about 5.5 m in length and 2 m in height.
facts.quote: Solo medía alrededor de 5,5 metros de longitud y 2 de altura

facts.statement: An adult Nanotyrannus lancensis may have weighed roughly 704 kg according to the specimen known as Bloody Mary.
facts.quote: El N. lancensis adulto pudo haber pesado alrededor de 704 kg, según el espécimen de Bloody Mary.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lethaeus individuals could have reached an estimated body mass of about 1 200 kg.
facts.quote: N. lethaeus, por su parte, era más grande; los individuos maduros pudieron haber alcanzado una masa corporal de aproximadamente 1200 kg.

facts.statement: Its skull was flat, square, and about 60 cm long, bearing sharp teeth and claws.
facts.quote: una cabeza chata y cuadrada con un tamaño cercano a los 60 centímetros de largo, contaba con garras y dientes afilados

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had a thin, low skull with small crests or horns just in front of the eyes, unlike the deeper skull of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus tenía un cráneo delgado y bajo, y pequeñas crestas o cuernos justo delante de los ojos.

facts.statement: The rear skull muscle attachment sites were large, suggesting it could laterally flex its head with great amplitude.
facts.quote: Los puntos de inserción muscular en la parte posterior del cráneo eran grandes, lo que sugiere que podía flexionar la cabeza lateralmente con gran amplitud.

facts.statement: Front upper‑jaw teeth lacked serrations, a condition called ziphodonty that is not seen in other tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la parte frontal de la mandíbula superior no eran serrados, a diferencia del resto, que a su vez se encontraban comprimidos lateralmente; condición conocida como zifodoncia que no se observa en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus possessed longer legs than contemporary taxa, indicating a pursuit‑predator lifestyle.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus tenía patas más largas que los taxones contemporáneos, lo que sugiere que era un depredador de persecución

facts.statement: Its forelimbs were proportionally larger than those of its tyrannosaurid relatives.
facts.quote: poseía extremidades anteriores que eran, tanto en términos absolutos como proporcionales, más grandes que las de sus parientes.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is the sole definitive member of the clade Nanotyrannidae.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus es el único representante definitivo del clado Nanotyrannidae

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lancensis had 14–15 teeth on each side of the upper jaw and 16 teeth on each side of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: N. lancensis tenía 14 a 15 dientes de cada lado de la mandíbula superior (maxilar) y 16 dientes en cada lado de la inferior (dentario)

facts.statement: Adult Tyrannosaurus rex had 11–12 upper‑jaw teeth and 11–14 lower‑jaw teeth per side.
facts.quote: T. rex, por su parte, tenía 11-12 dientes posicionados en su mandíbula superior y 11-14 en la inferior

facts.statement: A small foramen in the quadratojugal bone at the rear corner of the skull is present in both the Nanotyrannus holotype and the specimen known as "Jane" but not in known adult tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: la presencia de un pequeño foramen, un agujero en el hueso cuadratoyugal, que está situado en la esquina posterior del cráneo. Tanto el holotipo como el ejemplar "Jane" poseen este rasgo, lo que sugiere que no es una deformidad, y además no es conocido en ningún espécimen de tiranosáurido adulto

facts.statement: Researchers argue that the number of teeth may vary individually and is not a reliable indicator of growth stage.
facts.quote: el número de dientes por lo tanto puede variar por factores individuales no relacionados con el crecimiento

facts.statement: Some scientists consider Nanotyrannus to be a distinct genus, while others view it as a juvenile form of Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: las diferencias que se citan para apoyar la validez de Nanotyrannus son rasgos ontogénica o individualmente variables

facts.statement: 3‑D models of the braincase show differences in blood‑vessel and optic‑nerve canal positions between Nanotyrannus and T. rex, which may indicate taxonomic distinction.
facts.quote: Modelos 3D de las cavidades del cerebro del cráneo holotipo y del cráneo de T. rex muestran que las posiciones de los vasos sanguíneos y los de los archivos adjuntos del nervio óptico no coinciden, posiblemente lo que sugiere una distinción entre Nanotyrannus y T. rex

facts.statement: In 2001 a juvenile tyrannosaur specimen nicknamed "Jane" (accession BMRP 2002.4.1) was discovered and was suggested to belong to the same species as the original Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: En 2001, se descubrió un tiranosaurio juvenil más completo (apodado "Jane", número de acceso BMRP 2002.4.1), que se sugirió pertenecía a la misma especie que el espécimen original de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: The discovery of "Jane" motivated a tyrannosaur conference on the validity of Nanotyrannus held at the Burpee Museum of Natural History in 2005.
facts.quote: Este descubrimiento motivó una conferencia sobre tiranosaurios centrada en la validez de Nanotyrannus, celebrada en el Museo Burpee de Historia Natural en 2005.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Currie and Williams, who had previously supported Nanotyrannus lancensis as a valid species, interpreted "Jane" as confirming that Nanotyrannus was actually a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Varios paleontólogos que previamente habían publicado opiniones a favor de N. lancensis como especie válida, entre ellos Currie y Williams, vieron el descubrimiento de "Jane" como una confirmación de que Nanotyrannus era, de hecho, un T. rex juvenil.

facts.statement: Peter Larson continued to argue that Nanotyrannus lancensis was a distinct but closely related species and suggested that Stygivenator (LACM 28471) might be a younger Nanotyrannus specimen.
facts.quote: Peter Larson siguió apoyando la hipótesis de que Nanotyrannus lancensis era una especie distinta pero estrechamente relacionada, y también argumentó que Stygivenator (LACM 28471), que generalmente se considera un ejemplar juvenil de Tyrannosaurus rex, podría ser un espécimen más joven de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: In 2006 a nearly complete tyrannosaur specimen found together with a ceratopsian was studied by Robert Bakker and Pete Larson, who identified the ceratopsian as Triceratops and the tyrannosaur as Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: A finales de 2011, se hicieron informes de noticias sobre el descubrimiento en 2006, de un nuevo espécimen de tiranosaurio prácticamente completo encontrado junto con un cerátopsido. Los especímenes fueron estudiados por Robert Bakker y Pete Larson en el sitio, quienes identificaron al ceratopsiano como Triceratops y al tiranosaurio como Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: The specimen nicknamed "Bloody Mary" has arm bones almost three feet long, and its hand bones are one and a half times longer than those of the T. rex specimen "Sue".
facts.quote: El espécimen, apodado "Bloody Mary", tiene brazos de casi 3 pies de largo, y se dice que los huesos de la mano son una vez y media más largos que los del espécimen de T. rex "Sue".

facts.statement: In 2020 the Montana Supreme Court ruled that ownership of the "Bloody Mary" specimen should go to landowners Mary Anne and Lige Murray, who agreed to sell the fossils to a U.S. museum.
facts.quote: En 2020, el Tribunal Supremo de Montana dictaminó que la propiedad del espécimen debía ser otorgada a los propietarios del terreno, Mary Anne y Lige Murray, quienes acordaron vender los fósiles a un museo estadounidense.

facts.statement: The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences acquired the "Bloody Mary" fossil in 2020 and later built an additional research laboratory to prepare, study, and exhibit the specimens.
facts.quote: El Museo de Ciencias Naturales de Carolina del Norte adquirió el fósil en 2020 y, posteriormente, construyó un laboratorio de investigación adicional para preparar , estudiar y exhibir los especímenes.

facts.statement: In 2025 paleontologists Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli published an initial description of "Bloody Mary" as a Nanotyrannus individual with a mature skeleton, providing multiple lines of evidence supporting the validity of the genus.
facts.quote: En 2025, los paleontólogos Lindsay Zanno y James Napoli publicaron una descripción inicial del espécimen «Bloody Mary» como parte de una revisión exhaustiva del género Nanotyrannus . Identificaron este espécimen como un individuo de Nanotyrannus con el esqueleto maduro y aportaron diversas pruebas que respaldaban la validez de este género.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli also described a second species, N. lethaeus, based on the specimen Jane, citing notable differences from N. lancensis.
facts.quote: También describieron una segunda especie, N. lethaeus, basándose en el espécimen Jane, debido a las notables diferencias entre este y N. lancensis.

facts.statement: The specific name lethaeus is derived from the Latin adjective of Lethe, referencing both the Hell Creek Formation where the specimen was found and the mythological river of forgetfulness.
facts.quote: El nombre específico de la segunda especie, lethaeus, proviene del latín y es el adjetivo de Lete, en referencia al río Lete de la mitología grecorromana, que fluye a través del inframundo (a menudo equiparado al infierno). El nombre alude tanto a la Formación Hell Creek, donde se encontró el espécimen, como a la función mitológica de beber del Lete: olvidar una vida anterior y reencarnarse.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lancensis specimens have 15 to 16 teeth per side in the upper jaw and 16 to 18 teeth per side in the lower jaw, whereas adult Tyrannosaurus rex had 11 to 12 upper and 12 to 13 lower teeth.
facts.quote: Los ejemplares atribuidos a N. lancensis presentan entre 15 y 16 dientes a cada lado del maxilar superior y entre 16 y 18 dientes a cada lado del dentario inferior, mientras que los ejemplares adultos de T. rex tenían entre 11 y 12 dientes en el maxilar superior y entre 12 y 13 en el inferior.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is reported to have proportionally larger hands with additional phalanges in the third metacarpal compared to Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus se distingue de Tyrannosaurus por tener manos proporcionalmente más grandes, con falanges en el tercer metacarpiano y en la morfología de la fúrcula.

facts.statement: Both holotype specimens of Nanotyrannus possess a small foramen in the quadratojugal, a feature also seen in Daspletosaurus horneri and an isolated quadratojugal from Alberta.
facts.quote: Otra diferencia citada en apoyo de la validez de N. lancensis es la presencia de un pequeño foramen en el cuadratoyugal. Los holotipos de ambas especies de Nanotyrannus presentan esta característica, que también se observa en el espécimen adulto de Daspletosaurus horneri y en un cuadratoyugal aislado de Alberta

facts.statement: A 2016 limb proportion analysis suggested Nanotyrannus specimens show varying degrees of cursoriality, which was proposed as a possible taxonomic difference from T. rex.
facts.quote: Un análisis de proporciones de extremidades publicado en 2016 sugirió que los especímenes de Nanotyrannus presentan distintos grados de cursorialidad, lo que se citó como una posible diferencia entre N. lancensis y T. rex.

facts.statement: The growth curves of other tyrannosaurids such as Tarbosaurus and Gorgosaurus do not match the morphological changes proposed for a Nanotyrannus‑Tyrannosaurus growth series.
facts.quote: las series de crecimiento de otros tiranosáuridos conocidas, incluidos Tarbosaurus y Gorgosaurus, no muestran los cambios morfológicos propuestos para una serie de crecimiento de Nanotyrannus-Tyrannosaurus

facts.statement: The specimen 'Jane' (BMRP 2002.4.1) assigned to Nanotyrannus lethaeus was estimated to have died between 8 and 14 years of age.
facts.quote: Zanno y Napoli concluyeron que otro espécimen de Nanotyrannus , Jane (BMRP 2002.4.1), al que asignaron a N. lethaeus , murió entre los 8 y los 14 años de edad.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli argued that the ontogenetic patterns required for Nanotyrannus to be a juvenile Tyrannosaurus are not observed in any archosaur, challenging the synonymy hypothesis.
facts.quote: un patrón ontogenético no observado en ningún arcosaurio que contradice los patrones de fusión esquelética observados en NCSM 40000

facts.statement: The authors noted that some bone proportions, such as larger arm, wrist, and hand bones, differentiate Nanotyrannus from Tyrannosaurus, and no known amniote shows absolute limb reduction.
facts.quote: Los autores no conocen ningún amniota que experimente algún grado de reducción absoluta de las extremidades, sino simplemente casos en los que las extremidades crecieron más lentamente que el resto del cuerpo y se volvieron proporcionalmente más pequeñas.

facts.statement: After the Zanno and Napoli paper, some paleontologists who previously doubted Nanotyrannus, including Thomas Carr, Steve Brusatte, and David Hone, accepted 'Bloody Mary' as a distinct species from Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Autores que habían publicado artículos cuestionando la validez de Nanotyrannus , como Thomas Carr, Steve Brusatte y David Hone, aceptaron que el espécimen "Bloody Mary" era una especie distinta de Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: Holly Woodward Ballard urged caution before fully accepting Nanotyrannus as a valid taxon, and Carr argued it should be considered a species within Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: otros paleontólogos, como Holly Woodward Ballard, instaron a la cautela antes de aceptar los hallazgos , y Carr y Brusatte objetaron la clasificación del tiranosáurido juvenil BMRP 2002.4.1 "Jane" como Nanotyrannus lethaeus; Carr opinó que Nanotyrannus debería considerarse una especie dentro del género Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Longrich and Saitta recovered Nanotyrannus as a derived tyrannosaurid, but its exact relationship to Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus and Zhuchengtyrannus remains unresolved.
facts.quote: El último trabajo de Longrich y Saitta recupera a Nannotyranus como un tiranosáurido derivado, pero sin resolver con respecto a Tyrannosaurus , Tarbosaurus y Zhuchengtyrannus.

facts.statement: Gilmore concluded in 1946 that Nanotyrannus lancensis was a species of Gorgosaurus, placing it in the family Tyrannosauridae, subfamily Albertosaurinae.
facts.quote: Gilmore en 1946 concluyó que Nanotyrannus lancensis era una especie de Gorgosaurus. Esto lo ubicaría en la familia Tyrannosauridae, en la subfamilia Albertosaurinae.

facts.statement: Bakker and colleagues argued that Nanotyrannus fell outside the division between Tyrannosaurinae and Albertosaurinae, representing a primitive lateral branch of tyrannosaurids, which would place it outside Tyrannosauridae depending on the definition used.
facts.quote: Sin embargo Bakker et al., argumentaron que estaba fuera de la división entre Tyrannosaurinae y Albertosaurinae, y representaba una rama lateral primitiva de los tiranosáuridos. Esto coloca a Nanotyrannus fuera de Tyrannosauridae, dependiendo de la definición precisa utilizada.

facts.statement: The left side of the reconstructed skull of "Jane" shows puncture marks on the upper jaw that have been interpreted as bite wounds from a conspecific.
facts.quote: El maxilar superior muestra marcas de punción que se interpretan como mordeduras de un conespecífico.

facts.statement: CT scans of Jane's skull confirmed that the puncture wounds were traumatic injuries that later healed.
facts.quote: Las tomografías computarizadas posteriores del cráneo de Jane confirmaron aún más la hipótesis del equipo, demostrando que las heridas punzantes provenían de una lesión traumática y que posteriormente habían cicatrizado.

facts.statement: The facial lesions on Jane differ structurally from parasite‑induced lesions found on the adult Tyrannosaurus specimen Sue, which occur on the lower jaw.
facts.quote: las lesiones de Jane eran estructuralmente diferentes de las lesiones inducidas por parásitos encontradas en la Tyrannosaurus adulta "Sue", y que las lesiones de Jane se ubicaban en su rostro, mientras que el parásito que infectó a Sue le causó lesiones en la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus fossils have been recovered from the Hell Creek Formation, which spans present‑day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus se encontró en la Formación Hell Creek, que abarca partes de los actuales Montana, Dakota del Sur, Dakota del Norte y Wyoming.

rejected.statement: Re‑examination in 1988 by Bakker, Williams and Currie moved the species to the new genus Nanotyrannus because of its small body size compared with other tyrannosaurids.
rejected.quote: moved the species to a new genus of tyrannosaurid, named Nanotyrannus in reference to its small body size compared to other tyrannosaurids
rejected.reason: numbers not in the quote: ['1988']

rejected.statement: In 2025 Zanno and Napoli described a mature Nanotyrannus lancensis skeleton (the "Bloody Mary" specimen) and named a second species, N. lethaeus, based on the "Jane" specimen.
